stories.teaser: GPS trackers now watch over half of Israel’s vultures
stories.headline: GPS trackers help Israel protect its vultures, with half the population now tagged
stories.why: Just over 100 vultures carry transmitters; about 60 more will be tagged this fall, aiming for 75%.
texts:
Every vulture in the sky over Israel matters.

The Israel Nature and Parks Authority just released two vultures in the Lower Galilee with new GPS transmitters. One flew toward Mount Carmel, the other to Gamla Nature Reserve. Just over 100 vultures, nearly half of Israel’s population, now carry trackers that help protect them.

“The transmitters are our eyes in the field,” says ecologist Dr. Ohad Hatzofe.

#Israel #Nature #Conservation #Wildlife

100+ vultures tracked. 60 more this fall. Goal: 75% of the population.

The Israel Nature and Parks Authority, working with Tel Aviv University researchers, is fitting Israel’s vultures with GPS transmitters so it can follow them and protect them from threats like poisoning. Two freshly tagged vultures were just released in the Lower Galilee.

#Israel #Nature #Conservation #Wildlife

How do you protect a bird that can fly across the whole country in a day?

You give it a GPS tracker. Nearly half of Israel’s vultures now carry one, and about 60 more will be tagged this fall with help from Tel Aviv University.

“The transmitters are our eyes in the field. Without them, we are blind,” says Dr. Ohad Hatzofe of the Israel Nature and Parks Authority.

#Israel #Nature #Conservation #Wildlife
stories.og_title: GPS trackers reveal where vultures fly after release in Israel

stories.teaser: A 25-ton, 2,000-year-old ritual bath moved in one piece
stories.headline: Israel moves a 2,000-year-old, 25-ton ritual bath in one piece
stories.why: Found in Kiryat Gat, the mikveh is evidence of the first Jewish settlement known in the area.
texts:
Imagine lifting 2,000 years of history with a crane, and not letting it crack.

Israel Antiquities Authority conservators spent two weeks reinforcing a Second Temple-era mikveh found in Kiryat Gat, then lifted all 25 tons with a 300-ton crane. When building in the neighborhood is done, it’s expected to return for public display.

“Once you lift a structure like this, there is no going back,” says senior conservator Eyal Kahu.

#Israel #Archaeology #History #Heritage

25 tons. About 4 meters across. Around 2,000 years old.

The Israel Antiquities Authority moved a Second Temple-era ritual bath from Kiryat Gat in one piece, using steel beams, protective wrapping and a 300-ton crane. Excavation directors say it belongs to the first Jewish settlement known in that area. It is planned to go back on public display in the neighborhood.

#Israel #Archaeology #History #Heritage

How do you move a 2,000-year-old room?

Very carefully. Israel Antiquities Authority teams braced a 25-ton ritual bath from Kiryat Gat with steel beams and foam, then lifted it whole.

“The day before an operation like this, you don’t sleep,” says conservator Eyal Kahu. “You’re under pressure because the responsibility is yours and there is no room for mistakes.”

#Israel #Archaeology #History #Heritage
stories.og_title: Israel moves 2,000-year-old mikveh intact in complex 25-ton operation

stories.teaser: Insulin pump tweaks help young people with diabetes fast safely
stories.headline: Simple insulin pump tweaks help young people with diabetes fast safely, Israeli study finds
stories.why: Shaare Zedek and JCT study of 80 young people: 84.5% finished with adjustments, vs 40% without.
texts:
For a teenager with type 1 diabetes, fasting on Yom Kippur can feel out of reach.

A study at Shaare Zedek Medical Center and the Jerusalem College of Technology followed 80 young people through 109 fasts. Those who adjusted their insulin pump settings beforehand were far more likely to finish safely, and no one had a life-threatening complication.

#Israel #Health #Diabetes #Research

84.5% vs 40%.

That’s how many young people with type 1 diabetes completed a fast safely with and without adjusting their insulin pump first, in a study by Shaare Zedek Medical Center and the Jerusalem College of Technology. The researchers followed 80 adolescents and young adults through 109 fasts. Published in the Journal of Diabetes Science and Technology.

#Israel #Health #Diabetes #Research

Can young people with type 1 diabetes fast safely? With the right preparation, many can.

Israeli researchers followed 80 of them through 109 fasts. Most who tweaked their insulin pump settings in advance finished without problems.

“The most important finding of the study is that there were no life-threatening complications among the participants,” says Dr. Floris Levy-Khademi of Shaare Zedek.

#Israel #Health #Diabetes #Research
stories.og_title: Can young diabetics safely observe Jewish fasts? Insulin pump tweaks can help, Israeli study finds

stories.teaser: Two Israeli mathematicians win the 2026 Wolf Prize
stories.headline: Two Israeli mathematicians win the 2026 Wolf Prize
stories.why: Prof. David Kazhdan (Hebrew University) and Prof. Joseph Bernstein (Tel Aviv University) share the mathematics prize.
texts:
Proud moment for Israeli science.

Prof. David Kazhdan of the Hebrew University and Prof. Joseph Bernstein of Tel Aviv University have won the 2026 Wolf Prize in Mathematics, for foundational work in representation theory, automorphic forms and algebraic geometry. They will receive it at the Knesset in June 2027.

#Israel #Science #Mathematics #WolfPrize

8 laureates worldwide. 2 Israeli mathematicians.

Prof. David Kazhdan (Hebrew University) and Prof. Joseph Bernstein (Tel Aviv University) share the 2026 Wolf Prize in Mathematics, for helping create geometric representation theory. About a quarter of Wolf laureates in physics, chemistry and medicine have gone on to win a Nobel Prize.

#Israel #Science #Mathematics #WolfPrize

Ever heard of the prize that predicts the Nobel?

The Wolf Prize is often called that, and this year its mathematics award goes to two Israelis: Prof. David Kazhdan of the Hebrew University and Prof. Joseph Bernstein of Tel Aviv University. They are honored for their role in creating geometric representation theory.

#Israel #Science #Mathematics #WolfPrize
stories.og_title: 'Predictor of Nobel Prizes': 2 Israeli professors win prestigious Wolf Prize

stories.teaser: A simple saliva test finds a hidden infection in newborns
stories.headline: Israeli newborn saliva screening caught a hidden infection that standard testing would have missed
stories.why: 48,556 newborns screened at Hadassah: 176 CMV cases found, 100 of which targeted testing would have missed.
texts:
Most of these babies looked perfectly healthy.

Hadassah Medical Center and the Hebrew University screened 48,556 newborns for congenital CMV, a leading cause of non-genetic hearing loss, using pooled saliva tests. They found 176 infected babies, and 100 of them would have been missed by the usual targeted testing. 11 went on to receive antiviral treatment.

#Israel #Health #Babies #Research

48,556 newborns. 176 cases found. 57% would have been missed.

Researchers at Hadassah and the Hebrew University tested babies’ saliva in pools for congenital CMV, a leading cause of non-genetic hearing loss. Pooling cut the number of lab tests by about 83% compared with testing each baby separately. Published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases.

#Israel #Health #Babies #Research

Could a quick saliva swab protect a newborn’s hearing?

At Hadassah Medical Center, nearly every baby born over three years was screened for congenital CMV. Of 176 infected babies, more than half had no obvious reason to be tested. Pooling samples cut lab tests by about 83%, making universal screening practical.

#Israel #Health #Babies #Research
stories.source_name: American Friends of the Hebrew University, Oct 2, 2026
stories.og_title: Routine Newborn Screening Could Catch CMV Before Problems Appear

stories.teaser: A film about Ethiopian Jews’ journey to Israel wins top Haifa prize
stories.headline: ‘Hager (Land),’ an epic of Ethiopian Jews’ journey to Israel, wins Best Israeli Film in Haifa
stories.why: Shmuel Beru’s film won Best Israeli Film and a cinematography award at the 42nd Haifa International Film Festival.
texts:
Some stories deserve the big screen.

“Hager (Land),” directed by Shmuel Beru, tells the story of Ethiopian Jews on a dangerous journey to Israel. It just won Best Israeli Film at the 42nd Haifa International Film Festival, along with an artistic achievement award for its cinematography.

An important chapter of Israel’s story, beautifully told.

#Israel #Film #EthiopianJews #Culture

Best Israeli Film, plus an award for cinematography.

That’s what “Hager (Land),” directed by Shmuel Beru, took home from the 42nd Haifa International Film Festival. The epic follows Ethiopian Jews on a perilous journey to Israel amid political upheaval and violence, a chapter of history many people outside Israel have never heard.

#Israel #Film #EthiopianJews #Culture

Do you know the story of how Ethiopian Jews came home to Israel?

A new Israeli film tells it. “Hager (Land),” directed by Shmuel Beru, won Best Israeli Film at the 42nd Haifa International Film Festival. It follows Ethiopian Jews on a dangerous journey to Israel, and also won an award for its cinematography.

#Israel #Film #EthiopianJews #Culture
stories.og_title: 'Hager (Land),' an epic story of Ethiopian immigrants, wins Best Israeli Film at Haifa fest

stories.teaser: Hebrew University scientists make ice 10 times stronger
stories.headline: Israeli scientists create ‘super ice’ 10 times stronger than regular ice
stories.why: Hebrew University’s BioPykrete absorbs about 70 times more energy before breaking. Published in Colloids and Surfaces B.
texts:
Ice that bends instead of shattering? It now exists.

Prof. Ido Braslavsky’s team at the Hebrew University reinforced ice with plant-based cellulose and an engineered protein. The result, called BioPykrete, is about 10 times stronger than regular ice and close to standard concrete under compression.

“Instead of shattering suddenly, the material can absorb a large amount of energy and deform gradually,” he says.

#Israel #Science #Innovation #Materials

10 times stronger. 70 times more energy absorbed before breaking.

That’s BioPykrete, a new ice composite from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem made of ice, plant-derived cellulose nanocrystals and an engineered protein that binds them together. The team sees it as a possible lower-carbon building material for the Arctic and Antarctic. Published in Colloids and Surfaces B: Biointerfaces.

#Israel #Science #Innovation #Materials

Could we one day build with ice?

Hebrew University researchers made ice about 10 times stronger by weaving it with plant nanofibers and a protein that acts as molecular glue. It’s an early proof of concept, but a striking one.

“The result changes not only the strength of the ice, but also the way it breaks,” says Prof. Ido Braslavsky.

#Israel #Science #Innovation #Materials
stories.og_title: Israeli researchers create 'super ice' 10 times stronger than regular ice

stories.teaser: The cranes are back: autumn migration begins at Agamon Hula
stories.headline: The first cranes land at Agamon Hula as Israel’s autumn migration begins
stories.why: Tens of thousands of cranes and hundreds of thousands of other migratory birds are expected in the coming months.
texts:
Every autumn, northern Israel becomes a giant rest stop in the sky.

The first crane families, mainly from northern Russia plus Finland and Estonia, have just landed at Agamon Hula. Tens of thousands more cranes and hundreds of thousands of other migratory birds are expected in the coming months.

“This year the cranes were a little late, and they’re finally here,” says field manager Inbar Shlomit Rubin.

#Israel #Nature #Birds #Migration

Tens of thousands of cranes. Hundreds of thousands of migratory birds.

The autumn migration has started at Agamon Hula in northern Israel, where the first crane families have arrived, many with young hatched last spring. The site, run by KKL-JNF, gives birds a safe place to rest and refuel on their long journey south.

#Israel #Nature #Birds #Migration

Have you ever seen a sky full of cranes?

The first ones have just landed at Agamon Hula in northern Israel, kicking off the autumn migration. Many more are on the way.

“The exciting return of the cranes each year reminds us of the importance of protecting nature,” says KKL-JNF chairman Eyal Ostrovsky.

#Israel #Nature #Birds #Migration
stories.og_title: First cranes touch down at Agamon Hula, signaling start of Israel's autumn migration

stories.teaser: Israel’s Tamar Steinberg, 20, is windsurfing world champion
stories.headline: Israel’s Tamar Steinberg, 20, wins the windsurfing world championship
stories.why: Gold for Steinberg and silver for Sharon Kantor at the iQFoil World Championship in Weymouth and Portland, UK.
texts:
Just 20 years old, and already a world champion.

Israel’s Tamar Steinberg won gold at the iQFoil windsurfing World Championship in Weymouth and Portland, UK. She won her first four races and led the competition throughout. Teammate Sharon Kantor took silver, and Daniela Peleg finished fourth.

What a day for Israeli sailing.

#Israel #Windsurfing #Sport #WorldChampion

Gold and silver for Israel.

At the women’s iQFoil World Championship in the UK, 20-year-old Tamar Steinberg won the title and Sharon Kantor, a silver medalist at Paris 2024, took second. Three Israelis reached the final, guaranteeing Israel two medals. Steinberg won her first four races and led throughout.

#Israel #Windsurfing #Sport #WorldChampion

How do you become a world champion at 20?

Ask Tamar Steinberg. The Israeli windsurfer opened the iQFoil World Championship with four straight wins and never gave up the lead, taking gold in Weymouth and Portland, UK. Israel’s Sharon Kantor took silver to make it a double celebration.

#Israel #Windsurfing #Sport #WorldChampion
stories.og_title: Tamar Steinberg won the 2026 world windsurfing championship

stories.teaser: Tel Aviv University finds a way to get antibodies inside brain cells
stories.headline: Tel Aviv University researchers develop a way to deliver antibodies into brain cells
stories.why: In a preclinical Parkinson’s model, the method significantly reduced harmful protein clumps in nerve cells. Published in PNAS.
texts:
Antibodies are some of medicine’s most powerful tools, but they usually can’t get inside our cells. Until now.

Prof. Ben Maoz and Prof. Uri Ashery of Tel Aviv University developed a way to carry antibodies into cells, including brain cells. In a preclinical Parkinson’s model, it significantly reduced harmful protein clumps in nerve cells.

“This is an important step toward expanding the therapeutic toolbox of modern medicine,” says Prof. Maoz.

#Israel #Science #Parkinsons #Research

A new way into the cell.

Tel Aviv University researchers wrap antibodies in a temporary synthetic mask and lipid nanoparticles, so they can enter cells and then get back to work. In a preclinical Parkinson’s model, the approach significantly reduced harmful protein clumps. It also showed promise in models of cancer and inflammatory disease. Published in PNAS.

#Israel #Science #Parkinsons #Research

What if antibody treatments could reach targets inside brain cells?

A Tel Aviv University team, working with Cornell University and the Technion, built a system to do just that. Early lab results in a Parkinson’s model are encouraging, though clinical trials are still ahead.

“We have developed a system that enables antibodies to reach targets that were previously beyond their reach,” says Prof. Ben Maoz.

#Israel #Science #Parkinsons #Research
stories.source_name: American Friends of Tel Aviv University, Sep 23, 2026
stories.og_title: Tel Aviv University Researchers Develop New Technology to Deliver Antibodies Into Brain Cells
